content.thinking: The student's code simply checks s == s[::-1], without ignoring case and spaces. So "Madam" reversed is "madaM" != "Madam", and spaces cause mismatch. Need confirm with run_tests maybe.
Now give a level 1 conceptual nudge. Must not include code. Mention that the check compares raw string, but assignment requires normalize case and spaces before reversing/comparing. Keep conceptual.

input.text: Right now your code compares the raw input line with its reverse, so any difference in uppercase/lowercase letters or in spaces will make it say NO. Think about normalizing the string first: palindromes are about the sequence of letters, so you should strip away the characters you are told to ignore and make all letters the same case before checking whether the remaining letters read the same forward and backward.

content.text: The failures come from comparing the original input directly: `"Madam"` reverses to a different case pattern, and `"never odd or even"` has spaces that don't line up in reverse. The fix is to normalize the string first — remove spaces and make the case consistent — before comparing it to its reverse.
